title: बाढीले शान्तिबजार डुबानमा परेपछि विस्थापित २७ परिवार टेन्टमा (तस्बिरहरू/भिडिओ)
content:
No ads found for this position गोरखा । बुढीगण्डकी नदीमा आएको बाढीले गोरखाको आरुघाट गाउँपालिका-५ स्थित शान्तिबजार बस्ती डुबानमा परेपछि स्थानीय बासिन्दा विस्थापित भएका छन्। बाढीले घर डुबाएपछि प्रभावित परिवारहरू अहिले घर छाडेर भुइँथानमा अस्थायी टेन्टमा बसिरहेका छन्। स्थानीयका अनुसार शान्तिबजारमा करिब ५३ देखि ६० घर बाढीको डुबानमा परेका छन्। बाढीका कारण घरमा बस्न नसक्ने अवस्था भएपछि स्थानीयहरू सुरक्षित स्थानमा सरेका हुन्। अहिले भुइँथानमा २७ वटा टेन्ट राखिएका छन्, जहाँ २७ परिवारले आश्रय लिइरहेका छन्। बाढीपीडित इन्द्रबहादुर आले मगरका अनुसार असोज २५ गते आएको बाढीपछि आफूहरू विस्थापित भएका उनले बताए । नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटीले असोज २७ गतेतिर टेन्ट उपलब्ध गराएपछि प्रभावित परिवारले अस्थायी बसोबासको व्यवस्था गरेका छन्। ‘शान्तिबजारका करिब ६० घर डुबानमा परेका छन्। अहिले हामी भुइँथानमा टेन्टमा बसिरहेका छौँ,’ उनले भने, ‘स्थानीय सरकारले पनि राहत दिइरहेको छ। अहिले खान र बस्नका लागि व्यवस्था ठिकै छ।’ उनका अनुसार स्थानीय सरकारले चिसो बढ्दै जाने भएकाले विशेषगरी वृद्धवृद्धा र साना बालबालिका भएका परिवारलाई कोठा भाडामा लिएर बस्न आग्रह गरेको छ। त्यसका लागि प्रतिपरिवार मासिक १५ हजार रुपैयाँसम्म उपलब्ध गराउने भनिएको उनले बताए। बाढीपीडित गौरी गुरुङले पनि अहिले अस्थायी शिविरमा बसोबास र खानपानको व्यवस्था तुलनात्मक रूपमा सहज रहेको बताइन्। प्रभावित परिवारलाई खाना, सुत्ने व्यवस्था तथा बालबालिकाका लागि कपडा उपलब्ध गराइएको उनको भनाइ छ। ‘अहिले हामीलाई मुख्य रूपमा खान र सुत्नका लागि व्यवस्था चाहिएको हो। त्यो भइरहेको छ,’ उनले भनिन्, ‘सानो बच्चा र वृद्धवृद्धा भएका परिवारलाई कोठा भाडामा लिएर बस्न रकम दिने कुरा पनि भएको छ।’ बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा स्थानीय सरकार तथा विभिन्न निकायबाट राहत वितरण भइरहेको भए पनि विस्थापित परिवारको दीर्घकालीन पुनःस्थापना भने चुनौतीपूर्ण देखिएको छ। अस्थायी टेन्टमा बसिरहेका परिवारलाई चिसोबाट जोगाउने, सुरक्षित आवासको व्यवस्था गर्ने र क्षतिग्रस्त घर तथा सम्पत्तिको यकिन विवरण संकलन गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता छ। बाढीले घर डुबाएपछि विस्थापित भएका स्थानीय अहिले तत्कालका लागि राहत र अस्थायी आवासको भरमा दिन बिताइरहेका छन्। उनीहरूलाई सुरक्षित रूपमा घर फर्कने अवस्था कहिले बन्छ भन्ने अन्योल कायमै छ। Gorkha. Local residents have been displaced after floods in the Budhi Gandaki River submerged the Shantibazaar settlement in Arughat Rural Municipality-5 of Gorkha. The affected families are now living in temporary tents on the ground after their homes were submerged in the flood. According to locals, around 53 to 60 houses in Shantibazaar have been submerged in the floodwaters. The locals have shifted to safer places after being unable to live in their homes due to the flood. Currently, 27 tents have been set up in the ground, where 27 families are taking shelter. According to flood victim Indra Bahadur Ale Magar, he said that they were displaced after the flood that hit on Asoj 25. After the Nepal Red Cross Society provided tents around Asoj 27, the affected families have made temporary accommodation arrangements. "Around 60 houses in Shantibazar have been submerged. We are currently living in tents on the ground," he said. "The local government is also providing relief. Arrangements for food and shelter are now in order." According to him, the local government has urged families, especially the elderly and those with small children, to rent rooms as the cold weather is getting worse. He said that up to 15,000 rupees per family will be provided for that purpose. Flood victim Gauri Gurung also said that the accommodation and food arrangements in the temporary camps are relatively easy. She said that the affected families have been provided with food, sleeping arrangements, and clothes for their children. "Right now, what we mainly need is food and shelter. That is happening," she said. "There has also been talk of providing money to families with small children and the elderly to rent rooms." Although relief is being distributed by local governments and various agencies in the flood-affected areas, the long-term rehabilitation of displaced families remains challenging. There is a need to protect families living in temporary tents from the cold, provide safe housing, and collect accurate details of damaged homes and property. Locals who were displaced after their homes were submerged by floods are now living on temporary relief and temporary housing. It remains unclear when they will be able to return home safely.

बताए । नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटीले असोज २७ गतेतिर टेन्ट उपलब्ध गराएपछि प्रभावित परिवारले अस्थायी बसोबासको व्यवस्था गरेका छन्। ‘शान्तिबजारका करिब ६० घर डुबानमा परेका छन्। अहिले हामी भुइँथानमा टेन्टमा बसिरहेका छौँ,’ उनले भने, ‘स्थानीय सरकारले पनि राहत दिइरहेको छ। अहिले खान र बस्नका लागि व्यवस्था ठिकै छ।’ उनका अनुसार स्थानीय सरकारले चिसो बढ्दै जाने भएकाले विशेषगरी वृद्धवृद्धा र साना बालबालिका भएका परिवारलाई कोठा भाडामा लिएर बस्न आग्रह गरेको छ। त्यसका लागि प्रतिपरिवार मासिक १५ हजार रुपैयाँसम्म उपलब्ध गराउने भनिएको उनले बताए। बाढीपीडित गौरी गुरुङले पनि अहिले अस्थायी शिविरमा बसोबास र खानपानको व्यवस्था तुलनात्मक रूपमा सहज रहेको बताइन्। प्रभावित परिवारलाई खाना, सुत्ने व्यवस्था तथा बालबालिकाका लागि कपडा उपलब्ध गराइएको उनको भनाइ छ। ‘अहिले हामीलाई मुख्य रूपमा खान र सुत्नका लागि व्यवस्था चाहिएको हो। त्यो भइरहेको छ,’ उनले भनिन्, ‘सानो बच्चा र वृद्धवृद्धा भएका परिवारलाई कोठा भाडामा लिएर बस्न रकम दिने कुरा पनि भएको छ।’ बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा स्थानीय सरकार तथा विभिन्न निकायबाट राहत वितरण भइरहेको भए पनि विस्थापित परिवारको दीर्घकालीन पुनःस्थापना भने चुनौतीपूर्ण देखिएको छ। अस्थायी टेन्टमा बसिरहेका परिवारलाई चिसोबाट जोगाउने, सुरक्षित आवासको व्यवस्था गर्ने र क्षतिग्रस्त घर तथा सम्पत्तिको यकिन विवरण संकलन गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता छ। बाढीले घर डुबाएपछि विस्थापित भएका स्थानीय अहिले तत्कालका लागि राहत र अस्थायी आवासको भरमा दिन बिताइरहेका छन्। उनीहरूलाई सुरक्षित रूपमा घर फर्कने अवस्था कहिले बन्छ भन्ने अन्योल कायमै छ। Gorkha. Local residents have been displaced after floods in the Budhi Gandaki River submerged the Shantibazaar settlement in Arughat Rural Municipality-5 of Gorkha. The affected families are now living in temporary tents on the ground after their homes were submerged in the flood. According to locals, around 53 to 60 houses in Shantibazaar have been submerged in the floodwaters. The locals have shifted to safer places after being unable to live in their homes due to the flood. Currently, 27 tents have been set up in the ground, where 27 families are taking shelter. According to flood victim Indra Bahadur Ale Magar, he said that they were displaced after the flood that hit on Asoj 25. After the Nepal Red Cross Society provided tents around Asoj 27, the affected families have made temporary accommodation arrangements. "Around 60 houses in Shantibazar have been submerged. We are currently living in tents on the ground," he said. "The local government is also providing relief. Arrangements for food and shelter are now in order." According to him, the local government has urged families, especially the elderly and those with small children, to rent rooms as the cold weather is getting worse. He said that up to 15,000 rupees per family will be provided for that purpose. Flood victim Gauri Gurung also said that the accommodation and food arrangements in the temporary camps are relatively easy. She said that the affected families have been provided with food, sleeping arrangements, and clothes for their children. "Right now, what we mainly need is food and shelter. That is happening," she said. "There has also been talk of providing money to families with small children and the elderly to rent rooms." Although relief is being distributed by local governments and various agencies in the flood-affected areas, the long-term rehabilitation of displaced families remains challenging. There is a need to protect families living in temporary tents from the cold, provide safe housing, and collect accurate details of damaged homes and property. Locals who were displaced after their homes were submerged by floods are now living on temporary relief and temporary housing. It remains unclear when they will be able to return home safely.

बाढीपीडित इन्द्रबहादुर आले मगरका अनुसार असोज २५ गते आएको बाढीपछि आफूहरू विस्थापित भएका उनले बताए । नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटीले असोज २७ गतेतिर टेन्ट उपलब्ध गराएपछि प्रभावित परिवारले अस्थायी बसोबासको व्यवस्था गरेका छन्।

‘शान्तिबजारका करिब ६० घर डुबानमा परेका छन्। अहिले हामी भुइँथानमा टेन्टमा बसिरहेका छौँ,’ उनले भने, ‘स्थानीय सरकारले पनि राहत दिइरहेको छ। अहिले खान र बस्नका लागि व्यवस्था ठिकै छ।’

उनका अनुसार स्थानीय सरकारले चिसो बढ्दै जाने भएकाले विशेषगरी वृद्धवृद्धा र साना बालबालिका भएका परिवारलाई कोठा भाडामा लिएर बस्न आग्रह गरेको छ। त्यसका लागि प्रतिपरिवार मासिक १५ हजार रुपैयाँसम्म उपलब्ध गराउने भनिएको उनले बताए।

बाढीपीडित गौरी गुरुङले पनि अहिले अस्थायी शिविरमा बसोबास र खानपानको व्यवस्था तुलनात्मक रूपमा सहज रहेको बताइन्। प्रभावित परिवारलाई खाना, सुत्ने व्यवस्था तथा बालबालिकाका लागि कपडा उपलब्ध गराइएको उनको भनाइ छ।

‘अहिले हामीलाई मुख्य रूपमा खान र सुत्नका लागि व्यवस्था चाहिएको हो। त्यो भइरहेको छ,’ उनले भनिन्, ‘सानो बच्चा र वृद्धवृद्धा भएका परिवारलाई कोठा भाडामा लिएर बस्न रकम दिने कुरा पनि भएको छ।’

बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा स्थानीय सरकार तथा विभिन्न निकायबाट राहत वितरण भइरहेको भए पनि विस्थापित परिवारको दीर्घकालीन पुनःस्थापना भने चुनौतीपूर्ण देखिएको छ। अस्थायी टेन्टमा बसिरहेका परिवारलाई चिसोबाट जोगाउने, सुरक्षित आवासको व्यवस्था गर्ने र क्षतिग्रस्त घर तथा सम्पत्तिको यकिन विवरण संकलन गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता छ।

बाढीले घर डुबाएपछि विस्थापित भएका स्थानीय अहिले तत्कालका लागि राहत र अस्थायी आवासको भरमा दिन बिताइरहेका छन्। उनीहरूलाई सुरक्षित रूपमा घर फर्कने अवस्था कहिले बन्छ भन्ने अन्योल कायमै छ।

Gorkha. Local residents have been displaced after floods in the Budhi Gandaki River submerged the Shantibazaar settlement in Arughat Rural Municipality-5 of Gorkha. The affected families are now living in temporary tents on the ground after their homes were submerged in the flood. According to locals, around 53 to 60 houses in Shantibazaar have been submerged in the floodwaters. The locals have shifted to safer places after being unable to live in their homes due to the flood. Currently, 27 tents have been set up in the ground, where 27 families are taking shelter. According to flood victim Indra Bahadur Ale Magar, he said that they were displaced after the flood that hit on Asoj 25. After the Nepal Red Cross Society provided tents around Asoj 27, the affected families have made temporary accommodation arrangements. "Around 60 houses in Shantibazar have been submerged. We are currently living in tents on the ground," he said. "The local government is also providing relief. Arrangements for food and shelter are now in order." According to him, the local government has urged families, especially the elderly and those with small children, to rent rooms as the cold weather is getting worse. He said that up to 15,000 rupees per family will be provided for that purpose. Flood victim Gauri Gurung also said that the accommodation and food arrangements in the temporary camps are relatively easy. She said that the affected families have been provided with food, sleeping arrangements, and clothes for their children. "Right now, what we mainly need is food and shelter. That is happening," she said. "There has also been talk of providing money to families with small children and the elderly to rent rooms." Although relief is being distributed by local governments and various agencies in the flood-affected areas, the long-term rehabilitation of displaced families remains challenging. There is a need to protect families living in temporary tents from the cold, provide safe housing, and collect accurate details of damaged homes and property. Locals who were displaced after their homes were submerged by floods are now living on temporary relief and temporary housing. It remains unclear when they will be able to return home safely.
